CB30: Golden Moments

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Relive and discover the classic Golden Moments of Carte Blanche, on the show's 30th Birthday

Unique Selling Point:
Happy 30th Carte Blanche. We celebrate with the moments you would pay money to see over again -- Derek with the All Black players; Ruda with the gorillas in Rwanda; the Matshela Koko moment where Devi catches ESKOM’s CEO in a lie; animals rescued from the Luanda zoo…the iconic, moving moments that made Carte Blanche.

Summary:
An entertaining sequence within a special narrative, highlighting the golden moments in the inimitable style of Carte Blanche.

Press Release:


The moments you would pay money to see over again -- Derek with Madiba; Ruda with the gorillas in Rwanda; the Matshela Koko moment where Devi catches ESKOM’s CEO in a lie... the iconic, moving moments that made Carte Blanche.

Script:


VO: For 30 years this iconic theme has signalled the opening of South Africa’s longest running current affairs show on television.

Derek: Good evening and welcome to the first edition of Carte Blanche

VO: Carte Blanche has given you the right to see it all.

Derek: Welcome back - tonight’s show takes us to different worlds in more ways than one.

VO: And these were some of the moments that set us apart as the number one show on Mnet for three unforgettable decades.

Zaa: The country’s best kept secret...

Bonita: Oh my Go-hahahaha!!!!!

Vasti Manser: sobbing

Ruda: This is the crossing into Gaza from Israel

Bongani: We travelled to the country this week to talk to Ukarainians torn between Moscow and Kiev

Derek Link: Where I’m standing right now was the centre of a war zone

Sound up: Crowds etc

VO: Carte Blanche was there as our country struggled for freedom

VO: We paid testament to the transformation of a nation…

Derek: Thank you for adding the Madiba magic

VO: and were graced with a very rare royal greeting

Derek: Mam, Carte Blanche South Africa, looking forward to your visit.

Queen Lizzie: Oh Thank you very much

Derek: Looking forward to seeing you in a couple of weeks time.

VO: And Devi’s endless stare into Lionel Richie’s eyes was rewarded with a duet

Lionel and Devi: Sing… My endless love

VO: Endless love was not what Dorothy Letlape had in mind. Her ID book was stolen and she found herself a married woman. // So we went in search of her mystery husband.

Derek: Good to meet you. Ah you know your wife? Dorothy, Sohail
Dorothy: Hi my husband how are you?
Sohail: I’m not your husband

Derek insert VO: Sohail admitted that he’d bought the marriage certificate from a man in the street.

Dorothy: No, let my husband to hold it.

Derek: Oh ok, can I carry the small one? I can see you’re going to be a demanding wife Dorothy

VO: Relationship problems don’t end in real life - when Carte Blanche visited the Egoli set, things got a bit heated.

Derek: Do you think they ever get carried away, get it together
Ruda: What do you mean on the set?
Derek: No, in real life
Ruda: Oh no don’t be silly, that’s like people saying you and I are married
Derek: That’s ridiculous… ha ha
Brumilda: Sorry Derek darling…
Derek: Brumilda…
Brumilda: You two timing B@##$$, I’ve seen enough..
Derek… Brumilda, I can explain, wait.. come back!!!!

VO: From the city of Gold, to the 21st century gold rush, net savvy entrepreneurs were staking their claims.

Mark: This is the uniform - this is how I go to work - the shoes are unusual

VO: Mark Shuttleworth became South Africa’s first internet Billionaire when he sold his company to Verisign for 3.5 Billion Rand

Mark: Part of this is about creating a South African dream

VO: And money can buy some dreams,//Mark bought himself a 20 million dollar ticket to become the first African in space

VO: And the South African flag took to the skies

Sound up: Rockets…



VO: But Heroes can fall from grace - Paralympic gold medalist, Oscar Pistorius, dashed the hopes and dreams of sporting fans when he shot and killed his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp.

Court footage

VO: Carte Blanche was at the forefront of changing legislation to allow cameras into the courtroom, and launched the Oscar Pistorius Trial Channel on DStv...

John: Welcome back to our live position here in Pretoria

VO: Dubbed the trial of the century.

Sound up: Jail door

VO: And in another sporting controversy, Carte Blanche revealed exclusive undercover footage of Kampstaaldraad - a grueling boot camp for the Springboks.

Joost: - I saw it as a laugh, it was fun, but sore.

VO: Right from the start Carte Blanche became the people’s watchdog,

Sound ups:
They don’t want me to talk to Carte Blanche
// Are you aware that these are actually counterfeits?
// So the police are not able to look after anyone? Don’t be cheeky my sister
//I think you better answer these questions, you not going to talk to us? No.

VO: and we weren’t afraid to ask Radovan Krejcir the tough question

Bongani: One of the allegations is that you took care of him?

Radovan: I taking care of him? I never see him.

Bongani: I’m Bongani from Carte Blanche, we want to ask you a few questions..

VO: Catching the bad guys is not an easy task.

Medunsa: Please don’t take my photos

Devi: While he screamed the workers closed the workshop door and surrounded us

VO: In Hamanskraal, busting a policeman taking a sheep in exchange for a favour, put a new spin on bribery and corruption.

Lies, damned lies

and dirty tactics

Devi: Did they tell you I must wait outside?

VO: And then there was Eskom’s Matshela Koko, who was rendered almost speechless by Devi, over more Gupta related shenanigans

Devi: So did you prepay?
Koko: I suspect that’s the case
Devi: Ja, but Mr Koko, you said no
Koko: I suspect that’s the case, let me read this
Devi: Have a look, but when I asked you you said no
Koko: I must …. I must…
Devi: I asked twice. Mr Koko we are not moving as quickly as you would like me to move on
Koko: no no no, but let’s say I made a mistake
let’s say that
Devi: not let’s say, you’ve made a mistake
Koko: Okay I made a mistake, let’s do that, let’s do that
Devi: Yes

Macfarlane Link: If you think you’re having a crappy day at work, it’s nothing compared to what I’m about to do.

VO: Macfarlane got down and dirty with the zama zamas who scrounge the sewers for scrap treasure.

Mac: We’ve found a couple of teaspoons, we found a knife.

Macfarlane:This is unbelievable, but it’s also the sad reality of what some people have to do, and the lengths they have go to, just to be able to feed their families.

VO: Often we ventured into the wilder side of life

Derek: Give us another kiss

VO: In War torn Rwanda, Gorillas still lived in the mist and Ruda had a very close encounter

Researcher: It’s okay he won’t harm you

Ruda: I’ve probably never been as frightened in my life.

VO: We monitored the precarious and fragile relocation of the Thukela elephants who were scheduled to be culled.

John: The good news is they are within the perimeter fence:

VO: Carte Blanche followed the rescue of thirty three circus lions from Columbia and Peru, to their new home in South Africa.

Tim Phillips: These lions have never ever rubbed against a tree before, that’s just magical.

VO: Through The Carte Blanche Making a difference campaign, we have raised over R130 million equipping and renovating paediatric facilities in 10 state hospitals.

Sound up …. Yay!!!!

VO: Stories captured in time, have kept us glued to our screens every Sunday evening for 30 years...

Bongani: We’re playing with the big boys now.

VO: Carte Blanche made television history over// and over again.

Claire: Wow!

Cyril: I believe that our country has entered a period of change.

VO: Because, truth brings change

FIN!!!!
PROMO 1: 15”

VO: Thirty years of Carte Blanche have flown by, dusted with time-stopping moments.

Sound up Devi singing: Lionel: Let’s time this
part..You’re every breath that I take...

VO: Featuring rogues to riches and heroes to zeros.

PROMO 2. 15”

VO: Celebrate thirty years as we reflect on our unforgettable highlights.
Carte Blanche.
A window on the world, a mirror to South Africa.

PROMO 3. 30”

VO: For thirty years Carte Blanche made television history and some moments remain etched in time.

Derek: Thank you for adding the Madiba magic

Devi singing with lionel… with you

VO: Right from the start Carte Blanche was the people’s watchdog

Derek: I think you better answer these questions

VO: and we weren’t afraid to ask tough questions

Bongani: One of the allegations is that you took care of him…

Celebrate our journey with us as we turn back the clock.
